problems.title: Proportional allocation is not the guaranteed greedy algorithm
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF p.6, Eq.(4); Appendix C, Corollary 1, PDF p.31; proof C.3, PDF p.32
claim: Appendix C attaches a \(1-1/e\) guarantee to the allocation discussion, whereas Eq.(4) uses proportional crop scores.
analysis: For two crops with \(100\) constant-score tokens each, scores \(1\) and \(1/99\) yield quotas \((99,1)\) and log utility \(0\). Feasible quotas \((50,50)\) give \(\log(2500/99)>0\). Thus the claimed positive multiplicative guarantee cannot be attached to that proportional allocation. A separately specified marginal-gain greedy procedure is not refuted.
result: The supporting algorithm-to-guarantee attribution is invalid; empirical usefulness of proportional quotas remains open.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: For positive sorted scores, initialize one token per crop and allocate remaining feasible tokens by maximal log-prefix marginal gain. Its diminishing marginal sequences justify the appropriate separable allocation argument.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a supporting allocation guarantee, without a counterexample to the overall empirical method.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Token coverage does not by itself control pruning normalization
problems.source_location: Appendix C, PDF p.31, Assumption 1, Lemma C.1, Theorem C.1 and proof C.2
claim: Appendix C passes from token similarity/coverage assumptions to a transformer-output preservation bound.
analysis: With zero queries, attention on \([e_1,e_1,e_2]\) gives \((2/3,1/3)\), while pruning one duplicate gives \((1/2,1/2)\). Perfect coverage of the removed duplicate does not preserve multiplicity or normalization. A fixed-shape Lipschitz argument needs a common lifted representation and a separate deletion bound. The unspecified remainder may absorb this example.
result: A proof bridge is missing; the full numerical theorem is not refuted by this control.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an incomplete supporting argument with an unspecified remainder, not an established large theorem contradiction.
problems.existing_correction_status: No validated correction is established for this item.

problems.title: Selection uses raw attention instead of the computed holistic score
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF p.6, Eqs.(3)–(5); llava/model/utils.py, lines 22–164
claim: Equation (5) selects holistic scores; `llava/model/utils.py`, `HoloV`, computes those scores but takes top entries from `patch_attn`. The mean-normalized crop term also largely cancels.
analysis: For duplicated \(e_1\) and one \(e_2\), attentions \((0.333,0.333,0.334)\) can rank the \(e_2\) token highest by attention while holistic scores favor \(e_1\). Away from degeneracy, crop normalization makes the diversity contribution nearly a common factor, with rounding boundaries still relevant. Repository issues #13 and #15 already discuss parameter insensitivity.
result: The released path differs from the score definition; historical parameter effects are not newly quantified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use the intended holistic score for selection and an explicitly defined crop aggregation that does not unintentionally normalize away the desired variation. No recovered benchmark result is established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a known-context release mismatch, not demonstrated central scientific damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Overflow quotas produce padding instead of feasible real tokens
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF p.6, quota redistribution; llava/model/utils.py, lines 100–157
claim: Section 4.1 specifies capacity caps and redistribution; the released function floors quotas and later pads short outputs without redistributing overflow.
analysis: Two crops of capacity \(2\), weights \((0.98,0.02)\) and budget \(3\) produce nominal quotas \((3,0)\). The path selects only two real tokens and pads a zero, although \((2,1)\) is feasible.
result: The overflow branch violates the stated quota rule. Nonoverflow behavior is unaffected.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Cap initial quotas by capacity, then repeatedly allocate remaining tokens to an eligible crop under a declared priority rule until the feasible budget is met.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded release allocation boundary, with no measured effect on the main results.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
